messages:
mike_infra: Heads-up: seen a sustained spike in preemptions in us-central over last 12h. price-optimized pools' availability dipped ~8% during peak; capacity-optimized held but cost ~12% higher. Thinking of a tiered bid policy: mark latency-critical routes capacity-optimized, batch routes price-optimized. Thoughts?

priya_sre: Agree on the tiers. Latency-critical = real-time chat + embeddings. We should reserve a small warmbuffer (8-12%) on capacity pools so we can absorb short surges without falling back. Also want a graceful drain handshake so we don't lose KV cache mid-request.

jason_ops: Can we do a two-step drain? On preempt notice -> 1) mark node unschedulable, 2) route existing sessions to warmbuffer nodes, 3) snapshot KV state if >0.5s diff, then let preempt. Avoid hard kills where possible.

mike_infra: @priya can you share the autoscaler flag/annotation you had in mind for the drain? Also thinking about region fallback rules: prefer same-region fallbacks (eu -> europe-west1), avoid cross-region unless no capacity. Egress/cost implications need to be explicit in policy.

priya_sre: Draft flag we can use on node pools: 
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    inference.redwood/graceful-preempt-seconds: "60"
    inference.redwood/bid-class: "capacity"  # capacity | price
```
Autoscaler behavior: when preempt notice received, set Node.Spec.Unschedulable, give 60s for session handoff, then evict. If handoff fails, auto-fallback to price pool for that session.

infra-bot: Preempt-notice: instance gke-usc-pt-07 received TERMINATE in 22s (source=cloud).

elaine_cost: Cost perspective: switching some routes to capacity-optimized increases GPU spend ~10-15% but reduces p95 tail and retry-related token replays. With retries reduced we actually save on egress + CPU during retries. We should model net cost per 1M tokens for both configs before full roll.

mike_infra: Good point. Proposal: implement a routing tag 'bid-class' on model routes. Routing layer checks route.bid-class -> uses capacity pool if set, else price pool. Policy: if capacity pool size < threshold (5 nodes) for 60s -> spill traffic to price pool and optionally degrade to smaller model.

jason_ops: Edge case: when nodes are preempted we see network reattach latencies of 10-25s that break long-lived TCP streams (grpc). Need connection brokering so clients can reconnect to a warmbuffered session token rather than requiring the old TCP link. Suggest adding a lightweight session broker in front of runtime.

priya_sre: Agreed. Implementation sketch: on drain, runtime snapshots minimal state to objectstore and registers session token with broker. Broker returns new endpoint to client which fetches state. If snapshot > 2s then route to cheaper model variant and mark session as degraded.

mike_infra: Can we automate warmbuffer sizing? e.g., make warmbuffer = max(10%, ceil(peak_5min * 0.1)) and have autoscaler keep that many nodes in 'standby' with bid-class=capacity and lower-utilization. Also add a nightly probe that tests price pool availability and records preempt rate.

jason_ops: Need a capacity probe job. Quick bash probe idea: 
```bash
# probe price pools for 1 minute availability
for zone in zones; do 
  gcloud compute instances create preempt-probe-$zone --preemptible --image=probe-img --metadata=probe=true
  sleep 1m
  gcloud compute instances delete preempt-probe-$zone --quiet
done
```
Collect success/fail and eviction time to feed into bid decision.

elaine_cost: Also track "cost per successful request" = total_gpu_cost / successful_responses over a window. If capacity reduces replays by X, it may be worth the premium. We'll run sims.

priya_sre: I'll prototype the two-step drain + broker in a canary for us-central and europe-west1. Canary plan: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% over 48h windows if metrics OK. Metrics: preempt_rate, p95 latency, retry_count, cost_per_1M_tokens, session_restore_success.

mike_infra: Rollout checklist:
1) implement node annotations + autoscaler patch (respect graceful-preempt-seconds)
2) routing tag support (bid-class) in edge router
3) session broker + KV snapshot API (S3-backed)
4) capacity probe job + cost simulations
5) canary in us-central + europe-west1 for 72h

jason_ops: Also add fallback rules: if both pools low capacity, fall back to on-demand dedicated for critical tenants (configurable by customer). That avoids mass degradation.

priya_sre: Will open PRs with prototype config and tests. Expecting to iterate on snapshot granularity.

mike_infra: thanks team. Launch the canary Monday 09:00 PT. Ping here when PRs are up. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploybot: canary deploy queued for us-central (5% traffic) by mike_infra at 09:00 PT on Monday.
